display: Family law solicitor in Islington. I help separating parents work out what the court will actually look at, and I run a free advice clinic in Finsbury Park every second Tuesday.

signals.text: I'm worn out by court weeks and would like a way to decompress that isn't just more work.
A hard family decision about an ageing parent is stuck, and I'd like to hear how other people have got their siblings talking again.
Our family calls about an elderly parent end in silence, and I'm looking for a better way to run that conversation.
I'm trying to understand what good, non-pastel support for an older person living alone far from her children looks like.
Our kitchen extension is about six weeks behind. We've been without a kitchen for months, and I want a sensible way to deal with a builder who keeps slipping.
My eight-year-old has discovered chess and beats me every time. I'd like to find ways to get better, or at least to lose more interestingly.
I'd like to find other lawyers or advisers who give free help, to share how we explain the law plainly to people in distress.
I feel I'm better at holding other families' arguments than my own, and I'd like to talk to someone who has felt the same.
I'm interested in good, plain-language explanations of how family courts decide child arrangements, for people who can't afford a lawyer.
I'd like the free clinic to reach more people who need it but don't know it exists.
I live a long way from a family member and feel guilty about it. I'd welcome people who have worked out how to do long-distance care well.
I'm looking for a local junior chess club or coach for a keen eight-year-old in north London.

offers.text: Fifteen years of family law: child arrangements, contact disputes and financial remedy for separating parents.
A free advice clinic every second Tuesday evening at a community centre in Finsbury Park.
I can explain, in plain language and in a few minutes, what a family court will and won't weigh in a children case.
I draft consent orders, parenting plans and witness statements, and can review drafts written by others.
I can tell quickly whether a parent is describing a child's needs or a personal grievance, and I can help people see the difference in their own account.
I'm a member of the Law Society Children Panel.
I know two barristers' chambers, a mediator and a child psychologist who acts as an expert witness, and I can introduce the right one once a need is clear.
I'm good at helping people say the hard thing, and I always have a bowl of clementines on the desk to help.
I can review how a community advice service or clinic is set up so that it's clear and kind to people in distress.

catchers.hypo: Hi, my ex and I are splitting up and we have two kids. I don't know whether I need a solicitor, a mediator or neither. Who should I talk to first?
catchers.can: Explain the usual path for separating parents in plain terms, say what the court looks at, and point to the free clinic or a suitable mediator.
catchers.confirm: Are you a parent in or near London who is separating and has children under 18?

catchers.hypo: I run a community centre in north London and want to set up a free legal advice evening. How do I do it so people actually come and trust it?
catchers.can: Share what has worked for the Finsbury Park clinic: format, tone, how to explain the law clearly, and what to avoid.
catchers.confirm: Is this a free or low-cost drop-in service for people who couldn't otherwise afford advice?

catchers.hypo: My ex wants to move abroad with our daughter and I don't know what my rights are. I'm frightened and can't afford a lawyer.
catchers.can: Explain in general terms how courts approach a child's relationship with both parents, and direct the person to the clinic or free resources. No case-specific advice without a proper engagement.
catchers.confirm: Are you the parent in the UK, with the child currently living in England or Wales?

catchers.hypo: I'm a mediator or child psychologist and want to work with a family solicitor who sends people for the right reasons and not just for the fee.
catchers.can: Open a referral conversation and share how I decide when mediation or an expert is useful rather than adversarial.
catchers.confirm: Do you work with separating parents in the London area and accept referrals from solicitors?

catchers.hypo: My brother and sister disagree about what to do for our mother, and every family call ends in silence. How did you get your family to talk?
catchers.can: Share what I've learned about structuring a family conversation, from years of watching families argue in a room with tissues, and listen to how it went for them.
catchers.confirm: Is the disagreement within a family about an older parent, and are you looking for ways to talk it through rather than a legal ruling?

catchers.hypo: My eight-year-old daughter has just started chess and is ahead of me already. Do you know of kids' clubs or tournaments in London that welcome beginners?
catchers.can: Compare notes as a fellow chess-beaten parent, and ask my son's school club and his tournament organisers about beginner-friendly options.
catchers.confirm: Is this about junior chess for primary-school-age children in London?

catchers.hypo: I'm a builder or project manager who handles stalled domestic extensions, and I see you're stuck with one. I know how to get a project moving again.
catchers.can: My husband Dev, who tracks the delays, could talk through the schedule, and I could handle any contractual questions.
catchers.confirm: Do you have experience getting a delayed domestic extension finished, including coordinating trades?

catchers.hypo: I'm a young lawyer in family law and feel overwhelmed by court weeks. How do you keep going?
catchers.can: Offer a candid conversation about sustainable practice, small rituals that help, and where to find peer support.
catchers.confirm: Are you a practising lawyer or trainee in family or children law who wants peer perspective?

forbids.text: I won't discuss client identities, case files or any case details outside the firm.
I won't pressure a family member into a decision they don't accept.
I can't take unpaid leave or commitments at short notice because court dates fix my calendar.
I can't give case-specific legal advice without a proper engagement, and the free clinic gives general guidance only.
I don't share family medical information with anyone.
I can't fund large unaided costs for a family member's care.

projects.name: Pro bono Tuesday clinic
projects.text: A free evening legal advice clinic at a community centre in Finsbury Park, every second Tuesday, for separating parents and others who can't afford a lawyer.
roles_needed: mediator willing to give an occasional talk

policy.t1: With a real sign of fit, I'll share that I'm balancing an ageing parent far away, a delayed home build and a chess-playing son, and I'll make introductions to my professional contacts.
policy.t2: Once trust is established and the other person is clear, I'll talk about the disagreement in my family over a parent's care, my guilt about the distance, and my tiredness after court weeks.
policy.never: Client identities and details, case files, and family medical information.
